pick.headline: Polish parliament outlaws Solidarity
pick.summary: On October 8, 1982, the Polish Sejm passed a law dissolving all existing trade unions, including Solidarity.
pick.significance: The ban formalised the suppression begun with martial law; the United States responded by suspending Poland's most-favored-nation trade status.
pick.fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of October 8, 1982, carried Rakowski's Sejm case for new unions of "unequivocally socialist character" and Paris AFP on spokesman Urban saying the bill that could outlaw Solidarity might be amended after ILO proposals.
